meanings.note: Imperative senti grabs a listener's attention ('listen / look').
Mi sento a casa ('I feel at home'); sentirsela (te la senti?, 'do you feel up to it?').

examples.trans: Listen, do you have a minute?

meanings.note: Ownership, age (avere venti anni), and idioms like avere voglia di.
Forms compound past tenses of transitive verbs.
Takes a before a noun/pronoun ('think about/of': pensare a tutto) and di before an infinitive.

examples.trans: I am thinking of coming back tomorrow.

meanings.note: Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.

mollare.gloss: to quit; to drop; to let go of

meanings.en: to quit; to give up on
meanings.note: Lively informal verb for walking away from a job, project, or habit.
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Invariable feminine noun.
Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Fare effetto a qualcuno means making an emotional impression on someone.

examples.trans: How does that make you feel?

meanings.note: Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.

meanings.en: to stop; to cut it out
meanings.note: Colloquial smettila! attaches feminine 'it' for 'stop it! / knock it off!'.
Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

meanings.note: Contraction of preposition su + masculine singular article il (sul set, sul serio).
In sul serio, forms the fixed adverbial phrase 'seriously / for real'.
Single Italian word covering both question 'why?' and answer 'because'.

examples.trans: I am laughing because it is funny.

meanings.note: First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Everyday word for feeling glad or satisfied with a situation.
Links a time clause or asks 'when?'.

examples.trans: When I get back, I will call you.

meanings.note: In entrare in azione, means swinging into action.
Location or state; in silenzio means quietly, in porta means in goal.
Director's cue starting a take on set; also an act or deed.

examples.trans: We swing into action right away.

meanings.note: Default masculine plural definite article, plural of il.
Possessive determiner/adjective; normally preceded by the definite article (il mio contratto, i miei avvocati).
Legal representative.

examples.trans: I am speaking with my lawyer.

sapere.gloss: to know (a fact or how to)

meanings.note: Knowing facts or answers (sa dov'è?, non lo so).
Followed directly by an infinitive (sai giocare?, 'do you know how to play?').

examples.trans: Do you know how to play foosball?

stare.gloss: to stay; to be; to live

meanings.note: Stai fermo ('stay still'), stare in porta ('play in goal').
Come stai?, sto scherzando (stare + gerund for ongoing action), sta a Milano ('lives in Milan').

examples.trans: I am writing a note right now.

sciogliere.gloss: to dissolve; to untie; to melt

meanings.note: Used legally in sciogliere un contratto ('to terminate/dissolve a contract').

examples.trans: They want to dissolve the contract.

meanings.note: Default masculine singular definite article before most consonants.
Written work or legal agreement; da contratto means under one's contract.
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Literally a sack; un sacco di + noun is a very common informal way to say 'a lot of'.
Masculine Greek-origin noun ending in -a in the singular and -i in the plural.
Friendly or impatient encouragement built from dare.
Also shouted as praise (Bravo! / Brava!); fare il bravo means to behave.
Written with an accent to distinguish it from reflexive/impersonal pronoun si.

examples.trans: Yes, I am coming right away.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction introducing contrast or surprise (ma guarda!, ma come?).

examples.trans: I wanted to come, but I am working.

meanings.note: Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Blunt colloquial insult for someone acting foolishly.

examples.trans: Do not act like an idiot!

meanings.note: Everyday borrowing checking understanding or signalling agreement.
Conversational contrast word, slightly weightier than ma.

examples.trans: It is nice, though it costs too much.

meanings.note: Adverb before adjectives (troppo italiana) or determiner/pronoun for excess.
Nationality adjective; lowercase in Italian.
Informal greeting.
Informal farewell.
